subject: Clarifying where customer inference data gets processed — regions, subprocessors, and deletion timeline
messages:
From: Ariel Brooks <ariel.brooks@stellarishealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@stellarishealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where does my data get processed (regions/subprocessors) and deletion SLA?

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the call earlier — Stellaris is interested in Redwood for our patient‑facing inference pipelines but our security and legal teams need a concise answer on a few items before we move to a pilot:

- Which cloud regions can we constrain inference to? Do you support region‑only execution for hosted customers?
- Which subprocessors see request payloads or model inputs/outputs (including cloud infra, monitoring, CDN, KMS)? We need a list for our vendor inventory.
- If we ask Redwood to delete all customer request data (and embeddings), what is the deletion timeline and what evidence do you provide?

Could you provide a short written response and any artifacts (subprocessor list, data‑flow diagram, deletion SLA) we can share with legal?

Appreciate it — Ariel
Ariel Brooks
Director, Data Privacy & Security
Stellaris Health

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does my data get processed (regions/subprocessors) and deletion SLA?

Hi Ariel — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR answers up front, followed by supporting details and attached artifacts.

1) Regions and region‑only execution
- Hosted customers can pin inference to geographic regions we operate (US‑West, US‑East, EU‑West, APAC‑SE). For Stellaris we can constrain inference to US regions only (you pick primary region in the project settings).
- By default our smart‑routing can fall back across regions for availability; for strict residency we enable "region_only" routing which prevents cross‑region execution. This is available on Dedicated and for Hosted with an addendum.

2) Subprocessors that may see request data (high level)
- Cloud compute: AWS EC2 (us‑west‑2, us‑east‑1), GCP (eu model shards for EU customers), Equinix Metal (Dedicated offering).
- Storage & logs: AWS S3 (short‑term request logs), optionally customer‑managed storage for Private deployments.
- Networking / CDN: Cloudflare (edge routing), limited headers only; we do not cache request payloads at edge unless explicitly enabled.
- Key management: AWS KMS / customer KMS integrations (bring‑your‑own keys supported for Private).
- Observability / ops: Datadog (metrics/traces), PagerDuty (alerts). These systems receive operational telemetry; request payloads are not sent to Datadog by default.
- Vendor list & roles: attached CSV (subprocessor‑inventory‑2028‑06.csv) maps which vendor accesses which data type.

3) Deletion timeline and evidence
- Customer request to delete all request data and embeddings for a project: standard hosted SLA is 72 hours to initiate and up to 7 days to fully purge replicated copies across backup/replication windows.
- For Dedicated customers: we can provide a 72‑hour purge guarantee as a contract item (we coordinate with our infra team to truncate KV caches, remove embeddings, and scrub short‑term logs).
- For Private / on‑prem: deletion is immediate under your control.
- Evidence: we provide a deletion confirmation PDF (signed by operations) and a scrub report listing object keys removed. Sample artifacts attached (redwood‑data‑journey‑matrix.pdf).

Notes on cross‑border movement:
- When you select a US‑only routing policy, inference is executed in US compute and model artifacts are pinned to US storage. Control plane metadata (billing events, audit‑level event ids) may transit through our control plane region for orchestration; we can minimize this and include it in a data processing addendum.
- If you rely on our global failover, requests may be routed to a compatible model variant in another region; we will surface that option in the console and it is disabled by default for "region_only" projects.

Next steps:
- I've attached the subprocessor inventory and a compact processing map. If helpful I can set up a 30‑minute handoff with our Compliance team (Marissa) and Product Security (Karthik) to walk legal through the artifacts.

Best,

Ariel / Legal team — looping Marissa (Compliance) and Karthik (Product Security) to answer your technical evidence requests. Short answers below plus links to artifacts:

- Do Datadog / Cloudflare see PHI?
  - Datadog: no PHI by default. We send aggregate metrics and traces; request payloads (inputs/outputs) are never forwarded to Datadog. We retain traces that contain request ids (no PII) for troubleshooting; these are stored as telemetry only.
  - Cloudflare: edge only handles routing and TLS termination; request payloads are not cached at the edge unless a customer enables request caching explicitly. Cloudflare logs contain request metadata (IP, paths, timestamps) and can be excluded per contract.

- 7‑day replication window: what remains?
  - During deletion we remove the primary objects and purge active KV caches within 72 hours. Snapshots/backups may exist for disaster recovery for up to 7 days; we run a scheduled scrub that removes deleted objects from backups according to our backup retention policy. The attached matrix shows the retention timeline per storage tier and our backup rotation cadence. For contract customers we can shorten this window via SLA.

- Deletion confirmation & contact
  - Example deletion confirmation: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/01A-data-processing-matrix#deletion-confirmation-sample (redacted).
  - Primary contact for operations evidence: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com (Compliance Manager).

Scheduling: Marissa and Karthik have availability today 4:00–5:00pm PT or tomorrow 10:00–10:30am PT for a focused handoff. Which works for you?

Thanks — we'll prepare the redacted deletion PDF and a short slide that maps which vendor touches which artifact type (inputs, outputs, logs, metrics) ahead of the call.

Regards,
